description:
Check whether customers are safe to contact by reading every do-not-contact signal the API can see and naming the one it cannot. For each customer id it reads the public record and reports three signals: notifications switched off, a do-not-contact tag (Do Not Service, No Marketing, DNS, opt-out...), and do-not-contact language in the customer notes. `contactable` is true only when none of those are present.

Notes are read clause by clause, so "we do not service gas" (about the shop's services) and "customer refused to pay" (narrative) do not suppress anyone. Two kinds of clause come back under `review` with the clause quoted, because neither verdict is safe without a human: a CONDITIONAL gate ("do not schedule without a deposit") and a REVERSAL ("removed from DNS"). A customer with `needs_review: true` is not cleared until someone reads the quoted clause.

Read this before any outreach. But note the hard limit: Housecall Pro's Do Not Service checkbox is a dashboard setting this integration cannot read, so it is always returned under `unverifiable`. A `contactable: true` therefore means "no suppression signal was found on the readable surface" - it is NOT a clearance to contact. Confirm the Do Not Service checkbox in Housecall Pro before reaching a customer.

customer_ids.description: Customer ids (cus_...) to check, up to 100. One API read per id.

name: hcp_contactability
